verifier_note: Reached every source live: 8 arXiv IDs (all resolved via the arXiv API), 8 GitHub repos via the GitHub API, 3 Hugging Face model cards, one Crossref DOI, and raw LICENSE files for RVC, so-vits-svc, seed-vc, DDSP-SVC and knn-vc - zero fabricated citations. Six findings are corrected and the systemic fault is attribution rather than invention: measured numbers pinned to the wrong system or config (seed-vc's 430ms/150ms belongs to seed-uvit-xlsr-tiny, not the SVC checkpoint; SVCC 2023's 2.6-vs-3.0 similarity pair is cross-domain only; SVCC 2025's system counts are the superseded arXiv v1), plus two stated development GOALS in the Beatrice card (RTF<0.2, ~50ms) reported as measurements. One licence claim is decisively wrong - knn-vc ships a modified MIT that GitHub classifies as NOASSERTION - and separately HQ-SVC's repo carries no LICENSE file at all, which the finding does not mention.

Both sit inside the goals list opened by 'Beatrice 2 wa, ika o mokuhyou ni kaihatsu sarete imasu' (Beatrice 2 is being developed with the following goals), and the 2025-08-31 release notes state 'RTF no mokuhyouchi o 0.25 kara 0.2 ni henkou shimashita' (changed the RTF TARGET VALUE from 0.25 to 0.2). The card also describes the i7-1165G7 machine as the developer's laptop. Verbatim and correct: MIT covers source code AND trained models ('kono repository nai no source code oyobi gakushuuzumi model wa MIT License no moto de koukai sarete imasu'); ~9 GB VRAM at default settings; ~40 min training on a GeForce RTX 4090; the 2025-08-31 v2.0.0-rc.0 release; and RVC + Beatrice v2 as the only families in w-okada/voice-changer v2, with MMVC, so-vits-svc and DDSP-SVC each tagged 'only v1' in that repo's supported-models list.

corrections.claim: The phrase 'may slightly reduce clarity' is presented as a quotation but does not appear in the README. The source says of CLUSTERING that 'relying solely on clustering can reduce the model's clarity and make it sound less distinct', and separately of FEATURE RETRIEVAL that 'the timbre leakage can be reduced, the enunciation is slightly better than clustering, but it will reduce the inference speed'. The hedge 'slightly' belongs to the feature-retrieval comparison, not to the clarity cost, so the composite quote understates the clustering penalty. Secondary caveat: the 2023-11-11 archive date matches pushed_at and the README line 'the warehouse will enter the Archieve state', but GitHub exposes no archive timestamp, so that date is inferred from the last push rather than directly attested. Everything else in the claim verifies verbatim, including the AGPL-3.0 licence read off the LICENSE file.

corrections.claim: The real-time numbers are attached to the wrong model. The README's real-time performance table has exactly one row - seed-uvit-xlsr-tiny (22,050 Hz, XLSR-large content encoder, HIFT vocoder, 25M params, 10 diffusion steps) - at 430 ms latency and 150 ms inference per chunk on the NVIDIA RTX 3060 Laptop GPU. The singing checkpoint seed-uvit-whisper-base (44,100 Hz, BigVGAN, 200M params) has NO published real-time measurement, and the real-time GUI auto-downloads seed-uvit-tat-xlsr-tiny by default. The generic '~300 ms algorithm delay and ~100 ms device delay' is a separate top-level sentence, and the README's own formula (Block Time x 2 + Extra context right) yields 380 ms for that tiny config, so the '~300 + ~100 = 430' arithmetic mixes two sources. Everything else verifies exactly: archived=true, GPL-3.0 LICENSE, 3,889 stars, push 2025-04-20, cloning from a 1~30 s reference, the SVC checkpoint at 44,100 Hz with explicit F0 conditioning, 'use 30-50 for best quality', the minimum-1-utterance / 100-step / 2-min-on-T4 fine-tune, and arXiv:2411.09943 'Zero-shot Voice Conversion with Diffusion Transformers' by Songting Liu.

verdicts.verify_note: DOI resolves: INTERSPEECH 2023 pp. 2053-2057, Baas / van Niekerk / Kamper. 5-minute quote and WER 6.29 vs 6.39 verbatim. LICENCE WRONG: LICENSE is MIT text plus an added clause, so GitHub reports SPDX NOASSERTION ('Other'), not MIT.

corrections.claim: The reference implementation is NOT plain MIT. github.com/bshall/knn-vc ships MIT text (Copyright (c) 2023 MediaLab, Department of Electrical & Electronic Engineering, Stellenbosch University) with an extra condition spliced into the notice requirement: the licensee must also 'spend at least 10 seconds thinking about whether the idea of copyright for Software actually makes sense the first time you download the Software'. Because of that added term the GitHub licence API returns key 'other' with SPDX 'NOASSERTION', and the repo displays as 'Other'. In substance it stays permissive and commercially usable, but no SPDX-based licence gate or SBOM will recognise it as MIT, so it cannot be recorded that way. Second caveat: this is a SPEECH voice-conversion method evaluated on LibriSpeech, so the '5 minutes of reference' law and the 6.29 / 6.39 WER pair are speech results - projecting them onto a minutes-of-target-SINGING budget is the lane's inference, not the source's. Everything else verifies: repo live (push 2026-01-16, not archived), DOI 10.21437/Interspeech.2023-419 resolves to INTERSPEECH 2023 pp. 2053-2057, authors exact, WavLM layer-6 kNN plus HiFi-GAN, both quoted passages verbatim, and the README naming the prematched vocoder 'the best model in the paper'.

Table 1 minutes/phrases exact; Task 2 is speech-only; 4-point scale; 26 subs incl. 2 baselines. But 2.6 vs 3.0 is the Task 2 pair - Task 1 target similarity is 3.4 with the same ~0.4 gap; 4.0/4.1 MOS appear nowhere in the text.

corrections.claim: Two numeric attributions fail. (1) SIMILARITY: '~2.6 best vs ground truth ~3.0' is the CROSS-DOMAIN (Task 2) case, not the challenge-wide best. The paper reports target-sample similarity of 3.4 in Task 1 versus 3.0 in Task 2 ('even the target samples suffer from such a drop (3.4 v.s. 3.0)') with 'a clear gap (around 0.4 points) between the target samples and the top system in both tasks' - so the best similarity achieved in-domain is ~3.0 against a 3.4 ground truth. (2) NATURALNESS: '~4.0 top vs ground truth ~4.1' is stated nowhere in the paper; naturalness appears only as a boxplot (Figure 2) plus the prose that T23, T07 and T02 'are in fact not significantly different from the natural samples'. The 2026 SVCC-2025 analysis paper recalls SVCC 2023 as 'both the ground truth recordings and top system achieved around 3.9 naturalness scores', which contradicts 4.0/4.1. Verified exactly: Table 1 gives IDM1 11.84 min / 150 phrases, IDF1 12.72 / 159, CDM1 4.31 / 161, CDF1 6.75 / 150; Task 2 trains only on 'the target speakers' speech data' with the model never seeing their singing; similarity is judged 'on a four-point scale'; 26 submissions including 2 baselines (24 participant submissions; 25 and 24 systems in Tasks 1 and 2).

verdicts.verify_note: Style-accuracy percentages, 7 teams, the 2025-04-28 / 06-30 dates and 3.7-vs-3.9 MOS are verbatim in the live v2. But the system counts are v1's: v2 (2026-05-28) evaluates 33 systems = 2 ground truth + 6 baselines + 25 submissions.

corrections.claim: The '26 systems evaluated (18 submissions, 6 baselines, 2 ground truth)' breakdown is arXiv v1 (2025-09-19) and is superseded. The live version, v2 dated 2026-05-28, states 'In total, we evaluated 33 different systems, which are composed of 2 ground truth, 6 baselines, and 25 submissions', with a footnote reading 'The initial paper only analyzed 26 systems, but we included more ablation studies in this paper'. Anyone resolving arXiv:2509.15629 today gets 33 / 25. Everything else verifies verbatim against v2: 'submissions from 7 different teams'; training data released April 28, 2025 and converted results due June 30, 2025; 'the difficult singing styles to model were breathy, glissando, and vibrato, achieving only 37.3%, 42.6%, and 43.9% style accuracy scores, respectively' and 'pharyngeal, mixed voice, and falsetto singing styles were the easiest to model, with 44.8%, 48.3%, and 48.8%'; and 'The top systems only achieved a naturalness and similarity score of around 3.7 and 70% respectively, far from the ground truth scores of around 3.9 and 90%'. Minor labelling nit: the paper calls these 'style accuracy scores' in its conclusion; 'XAB' is its name for the traditional similarity test discussed under limitations, not an explicit tag on those percentages.
